title: What If Gravity Switched Off for 5 Seconds?
description:
Earth moves around the Sun at about 30 km every second. If gravity switched off for five seconds, Earth would fly about 150 km in a straight line, but over such a short stretch its curved orbit is almost straight anyway: it would end up only about 7 cm off its normal path. The real danger is closer to home. With no gravity, nothing slows a jump: push off the ground at about 2 m/s and you keep rising for the full five seconds, roughly 10 metres up, with nothing to stop you falling when gravity returns.

Sources: NASA Earth fact sheet (orbital speed 29.8 km/s, distance 149.6 million km); deviation = v^2 t^2 / 2R (our own calculation); typical standing-jump take-off speed about 2-2.5 m/s.
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations. This is a thought experiment.
